title: Madam Walker's Sunday house and the dicties
summary: She went every Sunday to Walker's house on St. Nicholas Avenue, among show people such as Lottie Tyler, Edna Thomas and Jimmy Daniels, the so-called dicties.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Madam Walker was one of my best friends. I used to go to her house every Sunday. Wasn't a Sunday I didn't -- didn't miss a Sunday. Lottie Tyler, who was my girl friend, Lottie Tyler and Edna Thomas and let me see, who else, we were considered the dicties, they called us dicties, you know. We were supposed to be the society of New York. Edna Thomas and Henry Branham, Jimmy Daniels -- no, that was before Jimmy's time. No, it wasn't. Jimmy used to go there. Jimmy Daniels, oh what is that boy's name? He's in Hawaii now.
Grand house, wasn't it over there?
Yes, oh, yes. But that was right on St. Nicholas Avenue. 280 St. Nicholas Avenue. Right there between 138th and 39th, on St. Nicholas.
All her friends were mostly show people.
Yeah, she hung out with show people.
In fact, whenever the society people would have the little concerts and things, she would always sing something, Lili Walker would.

Yeah. She couldn't -- and then she didn't do too bad at that. She sang -- she would sing a song, always, Lili Walker. And let me see now, what else? So, I've done my vaudeville now -- I mean my show and vaudeville in New York, haven't I?
